newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cascade busy as stock slumps. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Cascade busy as stock slumps. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects date from Oct 10 to Oct 11.)
Cascade Communications options were busy on four exchanges Friday as investors adjusted to a sharp drop in the stock price.
By 1010 CDT (1510 GMT), Cascade shares were down 10 at 76-1/2 on eight million shares. It hit a low of 74-3/4.
Traders said activity in both calls and puts was hectic, with investors both exiting positions and putting on new positions.
Cascade options trade on the American Stock Exchange, the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the Pacific Stock Exchange and the Philadelphia Stock Exchange.
"We're really busy. All calls and puts are trading," said a trader at the CBOE. He said no particular strategies were emerging in early trade.
He added that because the options trade on four exchanges, pricing the options was difficult because they were moving so sharply.
"It makes you crazy," he said.
Marty Kearney at PTI Securities added: "You have a real problem with everybody keeping the market up-to-date on a fast moving stock."

He said that occasionally the markets for the options will be tighter than for the underlying stock, but if the bid/ask on the underlying expands, some bid/ask spreads can expand to equal that of the underlying.
"It's pretty tight right now," he said of the market for both Cascade shares and options.

The most active Cascade option was the October 80 call, which traded more than 2,500 contracts. On the Philadelphia stock exchange, where the bulk of the options crossed, the option was down six at 1-5/8. The bid/ask was 1-7/16/1-11/16.
The October 80 call had open interest of 3,450.
Other active Cascade options included the October 75 and 80 call and put and the November 75 call and put.
On the Pacific Stock Exchange, the Cascade January 80 and 85 calls traded 140 and 100 contracts, respectively.
On Thursday, Cascade reported a surge in third quarter profits, to $0.21 per share from $).07 in the 1995 third quarter.
But the numbers still fell short of Wall Street expectations, and analysts said the disappointment lay in comparing Cascade's sequential quarterly earnings growth.
On Friday, SoundView Financial raised its 1996 and 1997 earnings estimates on Cascade.
In other trading, several Intel Corp were active as the stock rallied after Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock to strong buy from outperform.
Intel gained 3-3/4 to 103-5/8 on more than six million shares by 1025 CDT (1525 GMT).

Among the options the October 105 call, November 105 call and January 95 put were active. Also, a spread of 2,965 contracts in the October 55 call crossed. -Gregory Crawford, 312/408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
